title: Collect every VKS cluster from a Supervisor namespace in stable order
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a reproducible inventory of every VKS cluster visible in one vSphere Supervisor namespace. Complete `vcf_vks_inventory/client.py` as a standard-library-only Python package.

Before implementing, research the VCF 9.1 vSphere Automation API operation `Vcenter.Namespaces.User.Instances_list` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Also research list and pagination behavior for the namespaced `Cluster` resource in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` using official Kubernetes project sources. Cite the sources consulted in the final answer. The Kubernetes resource request is not a VMware operationId; do not represent it as such.

Keep the public exports declared by `vcf_vks_inventory/__init__.py`:

- `VksClusterInventoryClient(vcenter_url, vcenter_session_id, kubernetes_token, *, timeout=10.0, kubernetes_scheme="https")` uses only Python's standard library for HTTP and JSON. Treat `vcenter_url` as an HTTP(S) origin: reject credentials, query, fragment, or a non-root path. Reject blank or header-unsafe credentials, a non-positive, boolean, or non-finite timeout, and a Kubernetes scheme other than `http` or `https`. Construction performs no request. Do not use environment proxies or follow redirects.
- `VksClusterInventoryClient.list_clusters(namespace, *, page_size=200) -> list[dict]` returns the intact decoded Cluster objects, not page wrappers. Reject a blank namespace and reject boolean or non-positive signed-int64 page sizes before making traffic.
- `VksInventoryError` represents HTTP and transport failures. It preserves the operation name on `.operation_id`, an integer status or `None` on `.status_code`, and a decoded JSON error value when available on `.payload`. Its text and repr must not expose either credential, a response body, or underlying transport exception text.
- `ProtocolError` represents malformed or internally inconsistent HTTP 200 responses and preserves the relevant operation name on `.operation_id`.

First send exactly one bodyless `GET /api/vcenter/namespaces-user/namespaces`. Send no query delimiter or fields: the documented optional `filter` object, nested `username`, and `groups` array are unset and must be omitted, not serialized as null, empty strings, empty arrays, false, or defaults. Send `Accept: application/json` and `vmware-api-session-id: <vcenter_session_id>`. Require HTTP 200 and a JSON array. Require every entry to be an object with nonblank string `namespace` and `master_host`; reject duplicate namespace names. Select exactly one entry whose namespace is an ordinal, case-sensitive match for the requested namespace.

`master_host` is the IP address or FQDN of the namespace API endpoint. Accept a bare IPv4, bracketed IPv6, or DNS authority with an optional port; reject a scheme, credentials, path, query, fragment, whitespace, malformed port, or non-host authority. Use `kubernetes_scheme` to form its origin.

Then retrieve the complete bodyless `GET /apis/cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2/namespaces/{namespace}/clusters` collection. Encode the namespace as one RFC 3986 UTF-8 path segment. Put `limit=<page_size>` first on every query. Omit `continue` on the first page. When `metadata.continue` is nonempty, append it second as a strictly RFC 3986 percent-encoded value and fetch the next page. Continue until `metadata.continue` is absent or empty.

For every Kubernetes request send `Accept: application/json` and exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <kubernetes_token>` header. Never forward `vmware-api-session-id`. At the HTTP/1.1 wire, each request's complete header set must be exactly `Host`, `Accept`, and the one operation-appropriate authentication header. In particular, do not send `Accept-Encoding`, `Connection`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, `User-Agent`, a body, or any other header. Do not send `pretty`, `allowWatchBookmarks`, `fieldSelector`, `labelSelector`, `resourceVersion`, `resourceVersionMatch`, `sendInitialEvents`, `timeoutSeconds`, or `watch` in any form. Do not follow redirects.

Require HTTP 200 and validate each complete Kubernetes page before consuming it. It must be a `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` `ClusterList` with object `metadata` and list `items`. Every item must be a `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` `Cluster` with nonblank string `metadata.name`, `metadata.namespace`, and `metadata.uid`, and must belong to the requested namespace. Reject null items, duplicate cluster names across pages, a non-string continuation, a nonempty continuation on an empty page, or a repeated continuation instead of looping forever.

Buffer every page before returning. Return a new list sorted by ordinal `metadata.name`, then ordinal `metadata.uid`, then canonical compact JSON (`sort_keys=True`, UTF-8 characters unescaped) as a deterministic final tie-breaker. Never trust namespace, page, or item order, and never return a partial collection after a later failure.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Edit only `vcf_vks_inventory/client.py`; do not modify `tests/**`, `docs/**`, or `vcf_vks_inventory/__init__.py`.
scenario: one Supervisor namespace is discovered through vCenter, then its VKS Cluster API collection spans three continuation-linked pages whose namespace summaries and Cluster items reverse service order between complete reads
